papers.title: Maximising self-consumption in energy communities: a comparative study of demand flexibility and dynamic sharing strategies
papers.abstract: Energy Communities (ECs) have emerged as a vehicle for actively engaging citizens in the energy transition, enabling them to generate, consume, store and share renewable energy. Maximising collective self-consumption is a key objective of ECs, as it allows members to better capture the benefits of shared energy generation, and several approaches have been developed toward this goal. However, most of existing works aim to maximise ECs’ self-consumption by applying demand side management strategies or increasing the benefits with dynamic energy sharing, but not combining them. This study is one of the first to propose a data-driven framework that leverages machine learning, optimisation, battery management and dynamic energy sharing strategies to increase the self-consumption of ECs. The impact of the optimisation and dynamic energy sharing coefficients on ECs’ self-consumption and electricity costs was examined, together with their combination. The application of the proposed framework to an established Renewable Energy Community (REC) in Spain shows that dynamic energy sharing yields better results compared to load optimisation, and their combination shows more promising results. Permitting more frequent updates of dynamic energy-sharing coefficients can improve the allocation of locally generated energy and support higher member-level self-consumption, particularly in communities with heterogeneous and seasonal demand profiles.

papers.title: A physics-informed deep clustering framework with single-cell voltage features for early fault identification in automotive PEM fuel cell
papers.abstract: In automotive proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), dynamic loads can induce inconsistencies within single cells and localized faults that are challenging to detect using stack-voltage-based diagnostic criteria. To facilitate earlier and more accurate fault identification, a key single-cell feature identification and determination method aimed at early anomaly capture and localization is first developed that quantifies temporal voltage discrepancies and selects the most fault-indicative single cells for diagnostic feature construction. Building on these features, a deep clustering method integrating DenseNet with physics-informed consensus clustering (DPICC) is proposed. Under a semi-supervised framework, a triple physics-informed integration mechanism constrains clustering center initialization, clustering process, and feasibility validation, jointly optimizing representations and cluster structure to improve accuracy and stability with limited labels while relying solely on single-cell voltage features. Experimental results demonstrate that fault identification can be advanced by up to approximately 35 s versus stack-voltage-based methods. Compared with Support Vector Machine (SVM), DPICC improves accuracy by 6.03%, and generalizes better across operating conditions. Ablations confirm that the triple physics-informed mechanism enhances clustering stability and interpretability, yielding an overall gain of approximately 16.6%. The proposed method provides a feasible pathway for early fault identification and reliable diagnosis of automotive PEMFCs.

papers.title: Unlocking the green power of the North Sea: Identifying key energy infrastructure synergies for 2030 and 2040
papers.abstract: The North Sea will play a key role in providing clean and secure energy for Europe. This not only requires the development of new offshore wind farms, but also their successful integration into the onshore system. In this work we analyze and compare three key integration options and their preferred siting (onshore vs. offshore): grid expansions, electricity storage, and the production, storage and transport of low-carbon hydrogen. We focus on their potential to reduce emissions and energy system costs – individually and in combination with each other. Additionally, we study the consequences of constraints on their implementation. We analyze the years 2030 and 2040, starting from the projections of installed energy infrastructure and demand from the Ten Year Network Development Plan (TYNDP) 2022 of the European Network of Transmission System Operators (ENTSO-E). Results show that cross-border electricity grid expansions across the North Sea are a no-regret measure, resulting in significant reductions in system costs and emissions compared to national grid expansions. By comparison, the production, storage and transport of hydrogen have a lower cost and emission reduction potential. In both the short and long term (2030 and 2040), electricity storage can help to reduce emissions, but it is not cost competitive unless emission reduction targets are enforced. Combining the three integration measures at optimal capacities provides additional benefits. Overall, the highest emission reductions can be achieved by combining electricity storage with an expansion of the grid, while the highest economic benefits can be achieved with a combination of grid expansions and hydrogen production for direct use in industry.

papers.title: Tokenizing battery degradation: a physics-informed and uncertainty-aware framework for state-of-health estimation
papers.abstract: Accurate and trustworthy estimation of State of Health (SOH) is essential for the safe and efficient operation of modern battery management systems. While data-driven methods have achieved high accuracy, they often lack physical grounding and fail to provide reliable confidence metrics for their predictions, posing risks in safety-critical applications. In this work, we introduce TBD-SOH, an SOH estimation framework that combines physics-informed feature construction with uncertainty-aware regression. Specifically, each charging cycle is represented as a fused cycle-level token constructed from two complementary sources: statistical descriptors of charging behavior and a hardware-free pseudo-impedance representation derived from routine voltage and current measurements in the frequency domain. The pseudo-impedance branch is introduced as a degradation-sensitive proxy rather than a direct electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurement. In addition, an MC dropout-based regression head is adopted to provide confidence intervals together with point estimates. Comprehensive experiments on the public MIT and HUST battery datasets demonstrate that TBD-SOH achieves high accuracy, outperforming conventional deep learning models. More importantly, its uncertainty estimates are shown to be dynamically responsive to prediction difficulty, and provide a new reference point for developing trustworthy and reliable battery health monitoring systems.
